tools.name: Agreement of change maps
tools.description: Where and when several maps of change dates agree (Zeit's zeit.agreement): choose two or more results with dates (LandTrendr's year of detection, CCDC, BFAST or CODED break dates...), from this series or others. A change counts by its calendar year; maps agree when their years are at most the tolerance apart. Gives the consensus year and how many maps back it: changes found by several algorithms are the ones to trust. The maps are put on the grid of the first one.

params.label: Maps of change dates
params.help: Tool results whose values are dates. The outputs are on the grid of the first one checked.

params.label: Tolerance (years)
params.help: Years two changes may be apart and still agree (0: the same year).

outputs.name: Share of the maps that agree

tools.name: BFAST
tools.description: Breaks For Additive Season and Trend (Verbesselt et al. 2010), as implemented in Zeit. Iteratively splits the series into trend and seasonal components and detects breaks in each. Needs a regular series with several observations per year and more than two years.

params.label: Min segment size
params.help: Minimum segment length, as a fraction of the valid observations.

params.label: Max trend breaks
params.help: Maximum number of breaks searched for in the trend component.

params.label: Max season breaks
params.help: Maximum number of breaks searched for in the seasonal component.

params.label: Harmonic order
params.help: Number of sine/cosine pairs in the seasonal model (capped at observations per year).

params.label: Significance level
params.help: A component is only searched for breaks when the OLS-MOSUM stability test rejects at this level.

params.label: Max iterations
params.help: Maximum trend/season re-estimation rounds (usually converges much earlier).

params.label: Min observations
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid observations are not fitted.

tools.name: BFAST Lite
tools.description: Single-pass multiple-break detection (Masiliunas et al. 2021), as implemented in Zeit. Fits one segmented trend + harmonic model and picks the number of breaks by LWZ. Faster than classic BFAST. Magnitude = the model after the break minus the model before it, on the first observation after the break.

params.label: Min segment size
params.help: Minimum segment length, as a fraction of the valid observations.

params.label: Max breaks
params.help: Maximum number of breaks searched for and reported.

params.label: Harmonic order
params.help: Number of sine/cosine pairs in the seasonal model (capped at observations per year).

params.label: Min observations
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid observations are not fitted.

tools.name: BFAST Monitor
tools.description: Near-real-time disturbance monitoring (Verbesselt et al. 2012), as implemented in Zeit. Fits a stable trend + harmonic model on the history period and flags the first date in the monitoring period where the OLS-MOSUM process leaves its boundary. History = everything before the monitoring start.

params.label: Monitoring start (year)
params.help: Decimal year where monitoring begins (e.g. 2018.5). 0 = automatic: the last 25% of the series. Clamped so the history and at least one year of monitoring fit.

params.label: MOSUM window
params.help: Moving-sum window as a fraction of the history length.

params.label: Monitoring period
params.help: Maximum monitoring length relative to the history (sets the critical boundary).

params.label: Harmonic order
params.help: Number of sine/cosine pairs in the seasonal model (capped at observations per year).

params.label: Significance level
params.help: Significance level of the monitoring boundary.

params.label: Min history obs.
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid observations in the history period are not fitted.

tools.name: BEAST (Bayesian changepoints)
tools.description: Bayesian Estimator of Abrupt change, Seasonal change and Trend (Zhao et al. 2019), as in Zeit (zeit.beast, a port of Rbeast's C code, the same results from the same seed): the series is decomposed into a piecewise trend and a piecewise harmonic season whose changepoints, how many and where, are sampled by MCMC and averaged over all the models instead of one chosen. What comes out is the probability of a change at each date, the most probable changepoints with their probability and jump, and the trend with its 95% interval: an alternative to BFAST that says how sure each break is, robust to noise and gaps. Irregular dates are averaged onto a regular grid first. Every pixel is its own MCMC: a whole image is slow; try the visible area, an ROI or fewer samples first.

params.label: Season
labels: Automatic (harmonic with 4 or more dates a year)
params.help: A harmonic season of a year fitted with the trend, and its own changepoints; none for annual series.

params.label: Grid step (years)
params.help: The step of the regular grid the dates are averaged onto, in years: 1/12 monthly, 1/23 16-day, 1 annual. 0 = chosen from the dates as Rbeast does (a day, half a month, a month or a week).

params.label: Max trend changepoints
params.help: The most changepoints the trend may have (Rbeast's tcp.minmax).

params.label: Max season changepoints
params.help: The most changepoints the season may have (scp.minmax).

params.label: Max trend order
params.help: The highest polynomial degree of a trend segment: 1 linear, 0 flat.

params.label: MCMC samples
params.help: Samples kept per chain (Rbeast's default 8000): more are steadier and slower; a pixel takes about 10 ms per 1000 samples and chain.

params.label: Chains
params.help: Independent MCMC chains, averaged (Rbeast's default 3).

params.label: Burn-in
params.help: Samples discarded at the start of each chain.

params.label: Thinning
params.help: One sample kept every this many.

params.label: Seed
params.help: The random seed: the same seed gives the same result (Rbeast's too).

tools.name: CCDC
tools.description: Continuous Change Detection and Classification (Zhu & Woodcock 2014), Zeit's port of the original MATLAB code. Fits harmonic models to every band of a surface-reflectance series (Landsat-style: blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2, optional thermal) with a quality band, and starts a new model when consecutive clear observations depart from the current one. Needs several bands per date (map them to the roles below) and real dates; a quality band (Fmask or Landsat QA_PIXEL) is strongly recommended. Break magnitude = jump between the segment models at the break over the detection bands (reflectance x 10000).

params.label: Reflectance units
params.help: CCDC's thresholds are defined on reflectance x 10000. Automatic: median <= 2 -> reflectance 0-1; median >= 6500 -> Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 digital numbers (x 0.0000275 - 0.2); otherwise already x 10000. Janus applies the files' scale/offset metadata first, when present.

params.label: Consecutive anomalies
params.help: Consecutive anomalous clear observations needed to flag a change (the original's 'conse').

params.label: Change probability
params.help: Chi-square probability of the change threshold over the detection bands.

params.label: Outlier probability
params.help: Chi-square probability above which a single observation is an outlier, not change.

params.label: Max coefficients
params.help: Maximum number of harmonic model coefficients per band.

params.label: Max segments
params.help: Segments kept per pixel.

tools.name: CCDC synthetic image
tools.description: The image CCDC's harmonic models predict for one date (zeit.predict_synthetic_image): every band, in the series' units, and the quantity the series shows (e.g. NDVI), free of clouds, gaps and noise. Each pixel uses the segment that covers the date (before the first, the first; after the last, the last). Runs CCDC first, with the parameters below.

params.label: Date
params.help: Decimal year to predict (e.g. 2019.5 = early July 2019); 0: the date shown on the map.

params.label: Reflectance units
params.help: CCDC's thresholds are defined on reflectance x 10000. Automatic: median <= 2 -> reflectance 0-1; median >= 6500 -> Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 digital numbers (x 0.0000275 - 0.2); otherwise already x 10000. Janus applies the files' scale/offset metadata first, when present.

params.label: Consecutive anomalies
params.help: Consecutive anomalous clear observations needed to flag a change (the original's 'conse').

params.label: Change probability
params.help: Chi-square probability of the change threshold over the detection bands.

params.label: Outlier probability
params.help: Chi-square probability above which a single observation is an outlier, not change.

params.label: Max coefficients
params.help: Maximum number of harmonic model coefficients per band.

params.label: Max segments
params.help: Segments kept per pixel.

tools.name: S-CCD (stochastic CCDC)
tools.description: Stochastic Continuous Change Detection (Ye et al. 2021), as in Zeit (zeit.sccd): CCDC's harmonic models of every band (trend, annual and semiannual cycles), started on the first stable observations as CCDC's and then carried forward by a Kalman filter instead of refitted, so they follow slow changes and a new image costs one update. A change is several consecutive clear observations departing from the model over the detection bands (green to SWIR2); at the end of the series, the latest anomalous observations are a change in progress, not yet confirmed: the near-real-time state for monitoring. Needs the six Landsat-style reflectance bands mapped and real dates; a quality band (Fmask or Landsat QA_PIXEL) is strongly recommended. Faster than CCDC on long series.

params.label: Reflectance units
params.help: S-CCD's valid range and magnitudes are defined on reflectance x 10000. Automatic: median <= 2 -> reflectance 0-1; median >= 6500 -> Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 digital numbers (x 0.0000275 - 0.2); otherwise already x 10000. Janus applies the files' scale/offset metadata first, when present.

params.label: Consecutive anomalies
params.help: Consecutive anomalous clear observations that make a change (the peek window).

params.label: Change probability
params.help: Chi-square probability of the change threshold over the detection bands.

params.label: Outlier probability
params.help: Chi-square probability above which a single observation is an outlier, left out of the model.

params.label: Max angle (degrees)
params.help: Largest mean angle of the anomalous observations' change vectors to their median: a change departs in a consistent direction, noise does not.

params.label: Max segments
params.help: Segments kept per pixel.

outputs.name: Monitoring state (last date)
classes: Waiting for a model after a change

tools.name: CODED (degradation)
tools.description: Continuous Degradation Detection (Bullock et al. 2020), as implemented in Zeit: the NDFI of every observation (spectral unmixing, Souza et al. 2005) is modelled over a training period, and observations falling well below the model afterwards are a change. A change after which the land is still forest is degradation (selective logging, understory fire); otherwise it is deforestation. Needs Landsat-style surface reflectance (blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2) with real dates; a quality band is strongly recommended.

params.label: Reflectance units
params.help: The unmixing endmembers are reflectances. Automatic: median <= 2 -> reflectance 0-1; median >= 6500 -> Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 digital numbers (x 0.0000275 - 0.2); otherwise already x 10000. Janus applies the files' scale/offset metadata first, when present.

params.label: Monitoring start (year)
params.help: Year the monitoring starts; the training period is the years before it. 0 = the training period starts with the series.

params.label: Training period (years)
params.help: Years of the training period, whose NDFI model the monitoring compares with.

params.label: Consecutive observations
params.help: Observations in a row beyond the threshold that make a change.

params.label: Threshold (RMSEs)
params.help: How far below the model, in RMSEs of the training fit, an observation must fall.

params.label: Years after a change
params.help: Years modelled as the land cover after a change, and the least time between two changes.

params.label: Min observations
params.help: Least observations to fit a model (training, or after a change).

params.label: Changes
params.help: Only drops of the NDFI (disturbances, as CODED), or rises too.

params.label: Max changes
params.help: Changes kept per pixel.

params.label: Forest NDFI
params.help: Forest where a model's mean NDFI is at least this (before: forest or not; after a change: degradation or deforestation). Closed forest is near 1; open woodlands are naturally lower.

params.label: Max cloud fraction
params.help: Observations whose unmixed cloud fraction is above this are left out (CODED: 0.05); 1 keeps them all.

outputs.name: NDFI change at the first change
Mean NDFI of the training period

tools.name: LandTrendr
tools.description: Temporal segmentation of annual series (Kennedy et al. 2010), as implemented in Zeit. Fits a sequence of straight segments and maps the greatest (or newest, fastest...) loss or gain event per pixel.

params.label: Event
params.help: Direction of change of interest. Orients the segmentation (Zeit's direction) and selects which segments become events.

params.label: Max segments
params.help: Maximum number of segments in the fitted trajectory.

params.label: p-value threshold
params.help: Models with a worse p-value are rejected.

params.label: Recovery threshold
params.help: Maximum recovery rate per year (1/years).

params.label: Spike threshold
params.help: Desawtooth dampening of single-year spikes (1 = none).

params.label: Best model proportion
params.help: Prefer the model with most vertices whose p-value is within (2 - this) times the best one.

params.label: Vertex count overshoot
params.help: Extra candidate vertices before pruning.

params.label: Min observations
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid years are not fitted.

params.label: Pick event by
params.help: Which event is mapped when a pixel has several (raster runs).

params.label: Min magnitude
params.help: Events smaller than this are ignored (raster runs).

params.label: Min duration (years)
params.help: Events shorter than this are ignored (raster runs).

params.label: Pre-event value threshold
params.help: Loss: ignore events starting below this value. Gain: ignore events starting above it. 0 = off.

tools.name: Mann-Kendall trend
tools.description: Mann-Kendall monotonic trend test with Sen's slope, ported from pymannkendall to C++ in Zeit. Hamed-Rao and Yue-Wang correct the variance for serial correlation (usual in EO composites); the seasonal variant (Hirsch & Slack) tests sub-annual series per season. The first map shows Sen's slope only where the trend is significant.

params.label: Method
params.help: Hamed-Rao is the usual choice for annual EO composites, which are serially correlated. Seasonal pools per-season tests for sub-annual series.

params.label: Significance level
params.help: A trend is significant when its p-value is below this.

params.label: Autocorrelation lags
params.help: Hamed-Rao / Yue-Wang only: number of first lags used by the correction (-1 = all).

params.label: Seasons per year
params.help: Seasonal method only: observations per cycle (12 monthly, 23 MODIS 16-day). 0 = automatic, from the dates.

params.label: Min valid observations
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid observations are left empty (raster runs).

tools.name: NDFI (spectral unmixing)
tools.description: Spectral mixture analysis (Zeit's zeit.unmix) of every observation into green vegetation, non-photosynthetic vegetation, soil, shade and cloud fractions, with the endmembers of Souza et al. (2005), and their NDFI: near 1 in closed forest, lower where logging or fire opened the canopy, below 0 on soil and pasture. Needs Landsat-style surface reflectance (blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2) with real dates. A raster run writes the NDFI as a series and opens it as a new layer, ready for LandTrendr, BFAST and the other tools.

params.label: Reflectance units
params.help: The endmembers are reflectances. Automatic: median <= 2 -> reflectance 0-1; median >= 6500 -> Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 digital numbers (x 0.0000275 - 0.2); otherwise already x 10000. Janus applies the files' scale/offset metadata first, when present.

params.label: Max cloud fraction
params.help: Observations whose cloud fraction is above this are left out (CODED: 0.05); 1 keeps every observation. The quality band, when set, is applied first.

params.label: Also write the fractions
params.help: Raster runs: also write the GV, NPV, soil and shade fractions, each as a series (opened as layers).

tools.name: Phenology
tools.description: Land surface phenology as implemented in Zeit (a port of phenofit): smooths the series, splits it into growing seasons, fits a curve to each season and derives its start (SOS), peak (POS) and end (EOS). Needs a sub-annual vegetation index series (e.g. NDVI/EVI, 8-16 day or monthly). Maps summarize the seasons per pixel (median, latest or a given year); dates are days of the year of the season's peak.

params.label: Curve
params.help: Function fitted to each season.

params.label: Season start/end
params.help: How SOS and EOS are read from the fitted curve. POS is always the curve's maximum.

params.label: Smoothing
params.help: Smoothing used to find the seasons (the curves are fitted to the observations).

params.label: Whittaker lambda
params.help: Whittaker only: larger = smoother.

params.label: HANTS frequencies
params.help: HANTS only: number of harmonics per year.

params.label: Min pixel amplitude
params.help: Pixels whose series varies less than this (water, urban, bare soil) are skipped. Use the index scale (e.g. 0.1 for NDVI, 1000 for NDVI x 10000).

params.label: Min season amplitude
params.help: Seasons with a smaller rise above their troughs are dropped.

params.label: Min season length (days)
params.help: Seasons shorter than this (trough to trough) are dropped.

params.label: Season mapped
labels: Season peaking in the year below
params.help: Raster runs: how the seasons of each pixel become one map.

params.label: Year
params.help: With 'Season peaking in the year below': calendar year of the peak (0 = latest).

tools.name: Smoothing
tools.description: Smoothed curve of the series on the chart, with Zeit's Whittaker smoother (penalises roughness, follows the real spacing of the dates and fills gaps with the curve) or Savitzky-Golay filter (local polynomial over evenly spaced dates; gaps are interpolated first).

params.label: Method
params.help: Whittaker handles gaps and uneven dates and is a common choice for vegetation indices.

params.label: Whittaker lambda
params.help: Larger = smoother (10 is light for a 16-day series, 1000 strong). Its meaning does not depend on the spacing of the dates.

params.label: S-G window (dates)
params.help: Odd number of observations in each local fit (made odd and capped at the series length).

params.label: S-G polynomial order
params.help: Order of the local polynomial (below the window length).

tools.name: SOM clustering
tools.description: Self-Organizing Map (Kohonen), as implemented in Zeit: unsupervised clustering of the pixels by their whole series. The map is trained on a sample of the area, then every pixel goes to the nearest neuron; neighbouring neurons hold similar series. The result is a cluster map; hover it to see the typical series of the cluster under the cursor on the chart. Good for a first look at what kinds of trajectories an area has.

params.label: Grid columns
params.help: Neurons per row of the map: columns x rows clusters (at most 12).

params.label: Grid rows
params.help: Rows of neurons of the map: columns x rows clusters (at most 12).

params.label: Training sample (pixels)
params.help: Pixels the map is trained on, drawn at random from rows spread over the area.

params.label: Training passes
params.help: Passes over the sample (online training: one update per pixel and pass).

params.label: Dates without a value
params.help: A pixel needs a value on every date: fill the gaps linearly between its neighbours in time (the first and last values repeat at the ends), or leave such pixels without a cluster.

params.label: Min dates with a value (%)
params.help: When interpolating: pixels with values on fewer dates get no cluster.

params.label: Random seed
params.help: Seed of the sample and of the training (same seed, same clusters).

tools.name: Tmask (cloud screening)
tools.description: Tmask (Zhu & Woodcock 2014), as implemented in Zeit: a robust harmonic model of each pixel's green and SWIR1 series flags the observations that are too bright in green (clouds) or too dark in SWIR (shadows) for their date, which a quality band often misses (haze, thin clouds, shadow edges). Needs the green and SWIR1 bands and real dates. A raster run writes the series shown without the flagged observations and opens it as a new layer. The model spans the whole series: after a sudden lasting change (a clearing) the observations can look like clouds to it, so check such pixels on the chart.

params.label: Reflectance units
params.help: Tmask's thresholds are in reflectance (0.04). Automatic: median <= 2 -> reflectance 0-1; median >= 6500 -> Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 digital numbers (x 0.0000275 - 0.2); otherwise already x 10000. Janus applies the files' scale/offset metadata first, when present.

params.label: Write the screened series
params.help: Raster runs: also write the series shown without the flagged observations (opened as a new layer).

tools.name: TWDTW classification
tools.description: Time-Weighted Dynamic Time Warping (Maus et al. 2016), as implemented in Zeit (the distance of the R package twdtw). Each pixel gets the class of the most similar pattern: drop pins on places you know (forest, crop, pasture...), add them below as classes and name them. A pattern may match any stretch of the series; matching dates far apart in time is penalised by the time weight.

params.label: Classes
params.help: One reference series per class, taken from a pin or the ROI mean. Drop a pin on a place whose class you know, choose it in the list and give the class a name. Several patterns may share a name (they are separate entries in the legend).

params.label: Time weight: steepness
params.help: Slope of the logistic time weight, per day (larger = sharper transition at the midpoint).

params.label: Time weight: midpoint (days)
params.help: Time apart, in days, at which matching two dates costs half a unit more than matching the same date.

params.label: Time measured
params.help: Between the dates: for patterns that cover the period of the series (a pin's whole series). Between days of the year (31 December and 1 January are a day apart): for patterns of one season, which then match that season in any year.

params.label: Max time apart (days)
params.help: Dates more than this apart are never matched. 0 = no limit. The time weight adds at most 1 per pair of dates: on series with large values (e.g. reflectance x 10000) only this limit keeps a pattern near its own dates.

params.label: Max distance
params.help: Pixels whose best distance is above this stay unclassified. 0 = classify every pixel.

params.label: Min valid observations
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid dates stay unclassified.

tools.name: Post-processing (classes)
tools.description: Cleans a classification, a categorical layer of one map or a map per date (a land cover series, a model's class map), as Zeit's post-processing: the short excursions of each pixel's classes removed first (forest, pasture, forest becomes forest three times: zeit.desawtooth_classes), then each date's map through a majority filter (zeit.apply_majority_filter) and a minimum mapping unit that merges the patches under a size into the neighbouring class with which they share the longest border (zeit.mmu_sieve, as GDAL's sieve: the map stays complete). A raster run writes the cleaned classes, opened as a new layer with the layer's class names and colours, and how many dates of each pixel changed. On the chart: the pixel's classes after the temporal filter (the spatial filters need the neighbours: raster runs).

params.label: Temporal: longest excursion (dates)
params.help: A run of up to this many dates of one class between two runs of another, the same before and after (A B A), takes that class (A A A). 0: off. Needs 3 dates or more.

params.label: Majority window
params.help: Each pixel takes the most common class of this window (odd: 3 = 3 x 3), its own on a tie. 0: off.

params.label: Majority iterations
params.help: How many times the majority filter runs (it stops early when nothing changes).

params.label: Minimum mapping unit
params.help: Patches of fewer pixels are merged, the smallest first, into the neighbouring patch of the longest shared border, taking its class (11 Landsat pixels are about 1 ha). 0: off.

params.label: Patches
params.help: Whether pixels touching by a corner belong to one patch.

tools.name: SNIC segmentation
tools.description: SNIC superpixels (Achanta & Süsstrunk 2017), as zeit.snic: the area divided into segments of pixels whose whole series are alike (each date, or each band of each date, is one value compared), grown from seeds on R snic's grids, as sits_segment does. A raster run writes the segments' labels, each segment's mean series (opened as a new layer) and the segments' polygons in a GeoPackage (opened as a vector layer), with their size, centre and mean of every value: ready to interpret by object, to extract series from, or to classify one sample a segment.

params.label: Values compared
labels: The shown band or index of every date
params.help: Shown: the series shown on the map (the band, or the normalized difference, with the quality band applied). Every band: all the bands of every date, so pixels are alike when all their bands are (more memory and time).

params.label: Seed spacing
params.help: Distance between the seeds, in pixels (sits_segment's default: 10): about the side of a segment.

params.label: Seed grid
params.help: R snic's grids: rectangular; diamond (a second grid shifted by half a step, the step scaled by 1.41); hexagonal (the column step scaled by 1.73); random (as many seeds as the rectangular grid, drawn at random).

params.label: Compactness
params.help: Larger: more regular, compact segments; smaller: segments follow the data more closely. The values' differences are in their own units: 0.5 (sits' default) for reflectance or an index in 0-1, about 5000 for reflectance x 10000.

params.label: Margin
params.help: The margin along the edges kept free of seeds, in seed spacings (0.5: half a spacing, R snic's default).

params.label: Tile size
params.help: The area is segmented in tiles of this many pixels a side, in parallel; segments never cross the tiles' edges. 0: the whole area at once (one core, and the whole area in memory).

params.label: Dates without a value
params.help: A pixel is compared on every date: fill the gaps linearly between its neighbours in time (the first and last values repeat at the ends), or leave such pixels out of every segment.

params.label: Min dates with a value (%)
params.help: When interpolating: pixels with values on fewer dates are left out of every segment.

params.label: Random seed
params.help: Seed of the random grid (same seed, same seeds).

params.label: Write the polygons
params.help: Also write the segments as polygons in a GeoPackage, with their size, centre and mean of every value compared (a column each, up to 1000), and open them as a vector layer.

tools.name: AR(1) trend (remotePARTS)
tools.description: Linear trend with AR(1) errors fitted by REML (remotePARTS's fitAR, Ives et al. 2021), in Zeit: a t-test of the trend that accounts for the autocorrelation of the series, a parametric alternative to Mann-Kendall. The first map shows the slope only where it is significant. Analysis > Trend test (PARTS) tests these trends over a region, accounting for the spatial correlation of the pixels.

params.label: Trend per
params.help: The unit of the slope: per year of the dates, or per observation as remotePARTS's default.

params.label: Harmonics
params.help: Pairs of harmonics (cos, sin) of the yearly cycle fitted with the trend, for sub-annual series (0 for annual composites).

params.label: Missing dates
params.help: Exact: observations k dates apart are correlated by rho^k. Ignored: the valid observations are taken as consecutive.

params.label: Significance level
params.help: A trend is significant when its p-value is below this.

params.label: Min valid observations
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid observations are left empty (at least the model's terms + 2).

tools.name: Recovery (LandTrendr)
tools.description: How each pixel recovered after its disturbance, as in Zeit (zeit.recovery_metrics): LandTrendr segments the annual series, the greatest (or newest...) loss is the disturbance, and its fitted trajectory after the trough gives the years to recovery (Y2R), R80P, the relative recovery indicator (RRI), the absolute recovery (ARI) and the year-on-year recovery (YrYr) (Kennedy et al. 2012; White et al. 2017; Frazier et al. 2018).

params.label: Event
labels: Loss (the index drops with the disturbance)
params.help: Direction of the disturbance: loss for indices that drop (NBR, NDVI, TCW), gain for those that rise (SWIR bands). Gains need the recovery level 'Fraction of the loss'.

params.label: Max segments
params.help: Maximum number of segments in the fitted trajectory.

params.label: p-value threshold
params.help: Models with a worse p-value are rejected.

params.label: Recovery threshold
params.help: Maximum recovery rate per year (1/years).

params.label: Spike threshold
params.help: Desawtooth dampening of single-year spikes (1 = none).

params.label: Best model proportion
params.help: Prefer the model with most vertices whose p-value is within (2 - this) times the best one.

params.label: Vertex count overshoot
params.help: Extra candidate vertices before pruning.

params.label: Min observations
params.help: Pixels with fewer valid years are not fitted.

params.label: Pick event by
params.help: Which disturbance is measured when a pixel has several.

params.label: Min magnitude
params.help: Events smaller than this are ignored.

params.label: Min duration (years)
params.help: Events shorter than this are ignored.

params.label: Pre-event value threshold
params.help: Loss: ignore events starting below this value. Gain: ignore events starting above it. 0 = off.

params.label: Horizon (years)
params.help: Years after the trough at which the recovery is measured (ARI, RRI, R80P, YrYr): the best of the fitted values of years horizon - 1 and horizon (Frazier et al. 2018).

params.label: Recovered at (fraction)
params.help: The fraction of the pre-disturbance value (or of the loss) a pixel must return to: 0.8 for the 80% of White et al. (2017)'s Y2R and R80P.

params.label: Recovery level
params.help: Pre-disturbance value: recovered at target x the value before (White et al. 2017; an index that is positive and drops, such as NBR). Loss regained: recovered once that fraction of the drop came back (any index, either direction).

params.label: Pre-disturbance years
params.help: Years averaged for the pre-disturbance value, up to the disturbance's start.

tools.name: EWMACD (monitoring)
tools.description: Continuous monitoring of every observation (irregular, cloudy dates welcome) with EWMA control charts, as in Zeit (zeit.ewmacd; Brooks et al. 2014): a harmonic model of the training years, refitted without the clouds an X-bar chart screens; the residuals of every date after them smoothed by an EWMA, which signals when it stays beyond its control limits: a disturbance below, a gain above. Subtle shifts (thinning, drought, pests) as well as clearcuts; the date the pixel came back within its limits is its recovery. The flags are those of Brooks' EWMACD script (the paper's, Earth Engine's Ewmacd).

params.label: Training ends before (year)
params.help: The first year after the training period: the model is fitted on the years before it and the monitoring starts with it. 0 = three years of training (Brooks' default). The training years should be stable: a pixel disturbed in them signals as soon as they end.

params.label: EWMA weight (lambda)
params.help: Weight of each new observation in the moving average: low values are slow and smooth (subtle changes, few false signals), 1 a chart of each date alone (Brooks et al.: 0.3; 0.1-0.5 comparable).

params.label: Control limits (sigmas)
params.help: The control limits in standard deviations of the EWMA; the flags count how many limits the EWMA is beyond.

params.label: Persistence (dates)
params.help: Consecutive dates a signal must last to count (Earth Engine's default 3); a shorter run keeps the state before it.

params.label: Harmonic order
params.help: Sine/cosine pairs of the seasonal model of the training years (Brooks et al.: 2).

params.label: Training screen (sigmas)
params.help: Training dates farther than this from the model (clouds, shadows) are left out of the fit and of the chart (an X-bar chart).

params.label: Monitoring screen (sigmas)
params.help: Later dates farther than this from the model are left out as gross anomalies; the changes must stay in. A clearcut larger than this on a smooth series is screened until it comes back within it: raise it for such series.

tools.name: Spectral unmixing (endmembers)
tools.description: Linear spectral mixture analysis with endmembers of the image, as in Zeit (zeit.unmix with a table of endmembers): the fraction of each endmember (vegetation, soil, water, shade...) in every pixel and date, from all the bands of each date, and the RMSE of the rebuilt spectrum (Adams et al. 1995). The endmembers are the bands of pins at the map's date. Observations the chart leaves out (no data, the quality band's mask) are left out. A raster run writes each fraction as a series, opened as a new layer for LandTrendr, BFAST and the other tools, and their means as maps.

params.label: Endmembers
params.help: The pure spectra the pixels are mixtures of: the bands of a pin at the map's date. Drop pins on places of a known, pure cover (dense vegetation, bare soil, water, shade...), add each here and name it. Two to six usually; at most one fewer than the bands without the sum-to-one constraint. Bands without a value in one of them (the quality band, a scene's empty bands) are left out.

params.label: Constraints
params.help: Fully constrained least squares (Heinz & Chang 2001) gives fractions from 0 to 1 that add up to one; without the constraints the fractions can be negative or above one where the endmembers do not describe the pixel (the RMSE shows where).

tools.name: Spectral unmixing (spectrum)
tools.description: Linear spectral mixture analysis of a scene of one band per wavelength (hyperspectral: EnMAP, PRISMA, EMIT, AVIRIS...), as in Zeit (zeit.unmix): the fraction of each endmember in every pixel and the RMSE of the rebuilt spectrum. The endmembers are the spectra of pins. The chart draws the spectrum the fractions rebuild and each endmember's part of it.

params.label: Endmembers
params.help: The pure spectra the pixels are mixtures of: the spectra of pins. Drop pins on places of a known, pure cover (dense vegetation, bare soil, water, shade...), add each here and name it. Two to six usually; at most one fewer than the bands without the sum-to-one constraint. Bands without a value in one of them (the quality band, a scene's empty bands) are left out.

params.label: Constraints
params.help: Fully constrained least squares (Heinz & Chang 2001) gives fractions from 0 to 1 that add up to one; without the constraints the fractions can be negative or above one where the endmembers do not describe the pixel (the RMSE shows where).

tools.name: Emerging hot spots
tools.description: Emerging hot spot analysis (ESRI's Space Time Pattern Mining; sfdep's emerging_hotspot_analysis), as zeit.emerging_hotspots: at every date the Getis-Ord Gi* z-score of each pixel (its neighbourhood within a radius, at that date and the dates before it, against the date's mean), a hot spot where it is significantly high, a cold spot where significantly low; then the Mann-Kendall trend of each pixel's Gi* and its pattern as ESRI defines them: new, consecutive, intensifying, persistent, diminishing, sporadic, oscillating or historical hot or cold spot. Where the values (losses, an anomaly, a count) concentrate and how that changed. A raster run writes the patterns (a categorical map), the Gi* of every date (opened as a new layer: hover it for a pixel's Gi* series), its trend and how many dates each pixel was a hot or cold spot. The neighbourhoods need the whole map: raster runs only.

params.label: Radius
params.help: The neighbourhood: the pixels within this distance, the pixel among them (1 and a square: the 8 neighbours, queen contiguity, sfdep's default). Wider finds wider clusters.

params.label: Neighbourhood
params.help: Square: (2 radius + 1) x (2 radius + 1) pixels. Circle: those whose centres are within the radius.

params.label: Dates before
params.help: The dates before each date also in its neighbourhood (sfdep's k, ESRI's neighbourhood time step): 1 smooths each Gi* with the date before.

params.label: Against
params.help: Each date's mean and deviation (as sfdep: a place hot against the others at that date), or those of every date together (a date high everywhere is hot everywhere).

params.label: Significance level
params.help: A Gi* is a hot or cold spot when its two-sided p-value is below this; the same level for its trend.

params.label: Trend test
params.help: The test of each pixel's Gi* series (intensifying, diminishing or persistent). The Gi* of consecutive dates share neighbours, so their series are autocorrelated: Hamed-Rao corrects for it.
